title: Do agents need to sleep?
abstract: arXiv:2611.02216v2 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM-based agents, which increasingly operate persistently across sessions and accumulate memory through interaction, already exhibit the familiar symptoms of unchecked plasticity: semantic drift, degraded retrieval precision, propagation of stored errors, and saturation of memory capacity. Drawing on the selectionist "ringing, resonance and renormalization" (RRR) account of sleep, we propose that each of its three phases maps onto an operation feasible in digital memory architectures. Engineers building stateful agents, meanwhile, are independently rediscovering the problems sleep evolved to solve: what to forget, and when to do the forgetting. From this we derive the falsifiable prediction that selectionist consolidation will outperform instructionist alternatives as memory stores grow large. translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型的智能体日益跨会话持久运行并通过交互积累记忆，它们已经表现出可塑性失去控制后的常见症状：语义漂移、检索精度下降、存储错误的传播以及记忆容量的饱和。借鉴关于睡眠的选择论解释——“回响、共振与再归一化”（RRR）理论，我们提出睡眠的三个阶段可以分别映射到数字记忆架构中可实现的操作上。与此同时，构建有状态智能体的工程师们正在独立地重新发现睡眠在进化过程中所要解决的问题：遗忘什么，以及何时进行遗忘。由此我们得出一个可证伪的预测：随着记忆存储规模的增大，选择论式的巩固机制将优于指令论式的替代方案。核心主张涉及持续学习本身的本质：可塑性是有代价的，对于任何在有限条件下持续学习的系统……
tldr: 该论文借鉴睡眠的选择论“回响-共振-再归一化”（RRR）理论，将睡眠的三个阶段映射为智能体数字记忆架构中可行的操作，并提出可证伪预测：随着记忆规模增长，选择论式记忆巩固将优于指令论式方法。
en_tdlr: Drawing on the selectionist "ringing, resonance and renormalization" (RRR) account of sleep, this paper maps sleep's three phases onto feasible operations in digital memory architectures for LLM-based agents, and derives the falsifiable prediction that selectionist consolidation will outperform instructionist alternatives as memory stores grow large.
